text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm kicking off a triage for log coverage gaps across API gateway, auth, console, billing, and runtime. Got a short backlog doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/log-coverage-playbook :eyes:
jonathan: ack, will skim before 3pm sync. Can we surface which gaps are customer-impacting vs internal only?
tim: I can run a quick query to count recent 5xxs and map to missing events. will post results in thread.
sara: FYI some billing events were removed during the invoice refactor, probably why customer audit traces look sparse. filing SE-4392 now.
ashley: tagging infra for KV-cache runtime logging — we currently drop request_id on cache hits, makes debugging replay impossible.
leah: +1. runtime should log cache.hit with request_id and model_variant. low effort.
infra-bot: scheduled job "log-coverage-scan" completed: 47 services scanned, 12 with schema mismatches. Details: https://redwood.internal/scan/2150001234
maya: summary from scan would be great. prioritize by customer-facing first (billing, auth, gateway).
jonathan: quick pri list suggestion: 1) auth (token exchange missing), 2) billing (invoice create/update), 3) gateway (rate-limit drop), 4) runtime (cache ids), 5) console (ui audit events). thoughts?
tim: agree on ordering. I'll open ENG-876 to track runtime fixes. linking sample query I used: ```sql
-- find requests without audit events
select r.request_id, r.service, r.status
from requests r
left join audit_events a on a.request_id = r.request_id
where a.request_id is null and r.timestamp > now() - interval '7 days';
```
sara: SE-4392 created for billing, assigning to @ashley. I'll add failing customer case as example (cust: acme-enterprises).
ashley: got it. I'll add the missing invoice.create event and include schema. plan: small release next Tue.
leah: for auth: token.exchange event missing 'client_id' field in old flows. I can add a schema migration and backfill if we agree on format. Proposed minimal schema: ```json
{
  "event_type": "token.exchange",
  "request_id": "<uuid>",
  "user_id": "<id>",
  "client_id": "<id>",
  "success": true,
  "ts": "<iso>"
}
```
maya: that schema looks good. Add a migration plan doc and timeline. Backfill should be safe if we mark source="migration" on synthetic events.
jonathan: small note — KMS-integrated calls to billing sometimes omit user_id when service account used. That affects audit completeness. We should mark service_account_id in the schema too.
leah: good catch. I'll add optional service_account_id field and update the backfill script to set it when present.
infra-bot: log-backfill job queued: backfill-runtime-cache-ids -> ENG-876 (eta 6h).
audit-bot: schema-change recorded: token.exchange v2 (added client_id, service_account_id). Review required by sec-eng within 48h. https://redwood.internal/schema/changes/2150001234
maya: next steps: 1) owners open tickets for each service (if not already). 2) tag customer-impacting in ticket. 3) add minimal schema and backfill plan. 4) weekly follow-up on Friday cadence. I'll take ownership of triage board.
jonathan: I'll update triage board columns and add a 'customer-impact' label.
sara: can we add automated validation in ingest to reject events missing required fields for customer-impacting flows? even if soft-fail with alert.
maya: yes, implement soft validation -> emit validation.alert for missing required fields. Only hard-reject for malformed JSON.
ashley: question on rollout — for billing backfill we have to coordinate with payments window. I'll put tentative deploy Fri 11pm PDT in SE-4392.
leah: backfill script (psuedo): ```bash
# fill missing token.exchange events
python tools/backfill_token_exchange.py --since 2024-01-01 --tag migration --dry-run
```
tim: after dry-run we should run sampling to verify events land in audit index. I'll do that once ENG-876 backfill completes.
maya: thanks all. I'll create a short notes doc and assign owners. Meeting at 3pm if anyone wants to jump on a call. :thumbsup:
